Recently, I bought an old Dell Poweredge R905, which is a 4u server from 2007-2008. The one I have has 4 Xeon E7330 2.4ghz CPUs, 128gb of DDR2 memory, 5 300gb 15k RPM drives, 2 1570w power supplies, etc.

The issue I'm having is with the expansion. As I got it, there were 7 pcie x8 slots unused, out of 8 total. I wanted to put a GPU, a wifi adapter, and a sound card into it so I could use it as a normal computer as well as for all the virtualization I am going to do with it.

The first problem I encountered was that all the pcie x8 slots were closed back, meaning that, while a GPU would be compatible there was a little plastic bit that prevented me from putting it into the slot. I fixed this problem by very carefully cutting out the plastic bit.

The problem I am having now is that the pcie slots only deliver 25w of power each, rather than the ATX spec of 75w (I believe?). I'm looking for inexpensive and simple solutions that wouldn't take too much modification - but I'm not afraid to get my hands dirty, and I have a large number of parts at my disposal already. This is the best solution I have come up with so far.

Add in a third power supply and used powered pcie risers to supply power. This would involve cutting out most of the case around the expansion slots, 3d printing a new section to replace it (this wouldn't be impossible, but it wouldn't be easy either), and then mounting a normal consumer PSU from some old system and using that to power the expansion slots. In order to do this, it would involve buying 3 powered risers, the rest I already have. Total cost, ~$30-40.

The cards I need to power are an EVGA superclocked 750ti 2gb, a Creative sound blaster x-fi titanium, and an Intel 7260 dual band ac wireless card with a pcie adapter. I'm not certain about the total power consumption of these parts, but I'm fairly certain it's less than 130w. I have multiple power supplies that have enough connectors for the risers, with different sizes and wattages from 180w to 500w.

I'll do my best to answer any questions I can.

Original post on pcmr: https://voat.co/v/pcmasterrace/comments/338283
I have a rather odd problem and I need some input on possible solutions (x-post from /v/pcmasterrace)

Your card should be able to be powered by the atx power supply. I've done this on a similar Poweredge 1900 with a radeon 4750, I cut the pci-e slot and plugged in the power connections onto the GPU. The card was detected by bios and worked.

There are no internal power connectors on the r900 series, it all goes through a power distribution board and then the motherboard. Also, there's no 6-pin or 8-pin connectors for the 750ti, so it has to go through the pcie slot.

Edit: did you mean the third PSU I'm thinking of putting in?
Yes, you will need to use another power supply to supply the 6 and 8pin for your graphics card.
